subject: environmental-science
title: Soil & Composting: Foundations
welcome_lead: Soil isn't just dirt — it's a living, busy material.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: soil layers, types, importance.

concepts.def: Top layer of Earth where plants grow.
Dark, rich part of soil from rotted plants.
A balanced mix — best for growing.
Upper soil layer where most life lives.

walkthroughs.body_html: Soil mixes minerals, water, air and humus (rotted matter). It teems with bacteria, fungi, worms and insects.
Sand drains quickly. Clay holds water but can waterlog. Loam is the best balance for most crops.
Topsoil is the upper layer. It's where roots and most soil life thrive. Losing it takes centuries to replace.

mcqs.q: Best soil for most growing is:
What is the difference between species richness and species evenness?
options: Richness is for plants, evenness for animals.
Richness counts how many species exist; evenness measures how balanced their abundances are.

Water vapour released from plant leaves to the atmosphere.
